einzeiler: Celebrating the life, legacy, and cultural impact of the late Dolly Parton.
kurzfassung: Rolling Stone editors remember the life and cultural impact of Dolly Parton following her passing at age 80. They discuss her ability to unite people across divides, her extensive songwriting catalog, and her deep ties to Nashville. The episode also highlights her meticulous preparation for her final farewell and recommends essential songs to revisit.
stichpunkte: Nashville mourns and celebrates the life of Dolly Parton after her passing at age 80.
Impromptu memorials pop up across Nashville, from murals to local businesses.
Dolly Parton served as a unifying figure who transcended genre boundaries and political divides.
She carefully prepared for the end of her life, recording material and organizing final projects ahead of time.
Her marriage to Carl Dean and her unseen battles with cancer and caregiving reveal a deeply private side.
Modern country stars like Lainey Wilson and Luke Holmes share aspects of her unifying appeal.
Her final public appearance took place at a truck store opening in Tennessee.
The hosts conclude by sharing a curated list of essential Dolly Parton songs to honor her catalog.

clips.hook: You do not mess with Dolly.
clips.text: Locals reacted with fierce loyalty when a cardboard cutout of the music icon was stolen from a local establishment.
The singer possessed a remarkable ability to playfully acknowledge public perceptions and maintain a sense of humor about herself.
Even the most celebrated entertainers face private struggles while looking after loved ones at home.
Rather than attending an elite gala, the legendary artist chose to connect with everyday fans at a commercial travel plaza.

clips.hook: Taking her incredible catalog for granted.
clips.text: Public perception often overlooked the staggering depth and emotional range of her thousands of recorded compositions.

beschreibung:
Dolly Parton’s death on Aug. 25 at age 80 after a quiet battle with cancer resonated around the globe. But it was especially acute in Nashville, where she lived, launched her career, and died. In a special tribute episode of Rolling Stone’s Nashville Now podcast, host Joseph Hudak and Rolling Stone Senior Writer Marissa R. Moss talk about the vibe of the city, what we’ve felt, and what’s to come. We also explain what Dolly’s final public appearance says about her life, share our favorite Dolly moments, and offer our thoughts on who in country music best embodies the Dolly spirit. It’s a remembrance of a woman, an artist, and an icon whose impact will be felt for generations, only on Nashville Now.

Country is Here… Nashville is Now.
